title: fix(verify): read a refused create's whole answer before calling it a hard failure
body:
Fixes #24498

Clause-②: no

Basis: the CRUD stage reads the same answer correctly. No accept set, export or published shape moves.

## What changed

`packages/verify/src/verify.ts`, `runCrudVerification`, the refused-create branch:

- The body is read once, in full. The verdict comes from a new private helper, `isValidationAnswer(text)`.
  - When the body is JSON with a string top-level `code`, a 400 is `needs-fixture` exactly when that code is `VALIDATION_FAILED`.
  - When the body is not JSON, or has no string `code`, the stage's original pattern (`VALIDATION_FAILED|Validation failed`, case-insensitive) is matched against the full text.
- The stored `detail` keeps its 280-character cut (`text.slice(0, 280)`), taken after the verdict.
- The rule is unchanged: a 400 validation answer is `needs-fixture`, and anything else is `create-failed`. No other status value, exit-code rule or verify stage is touched.

**The shape was measured, not guessed.** A real in-process stack (`bootStack`, this branch, after the dependency closure was built) answered a create refused by a script rule with `400` and a 755-character body whose keys are `["error","code","fields","object"]`. The `"code":"VALIDATION_FAILED"` key starts at character 324. That is the flat envelope `packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts` builds for the validation arm (`error` = the app's message, then `code`, `fields`, `object`). It is also the top-level `code` that the sibling stages already read off this same door (`reference-shape.ts`, `delete-behavior.ts`, `unique-scope.ts`). The test fixture uses that measured key order and `fields` entry shape.

## Before and after: the stored row for a long validation answer, measured

The probe is a throwaway script, not committed. It boots one real stack with one object whose script rule (CEL `true`, events insert and update) refuses every create with a three-sentence message, like hotcrm's forecast rule. It then runs `runCrudVerification` over that app. "Before" imports `verify.ts` exactly as it is at base `6b42b6bc8`. "After" imports it at `3024fa2b7`.

| run | `verify.ts` | status | code | `detail` length | summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | base `6b42b6bc8` | `create-failed` | 400 | 280 | `createFailed: 1, needsFixture: 0` |
| after | `3024fa2b7` | `needs-fixture` | 400 | 280 | `createFailed: 0, needsFixture: 1` |

The stored `detail` is byte-identical in both rows. It ends `... reconcile the three amounts, th`, before the `code` key at character 324. Only the verdict moves.

The optional hotcrm re-run was **not done**. The hotcrm checkout has no `node_modules`. Running `os verify` there with this branch's build means installing its 18.0.0-next.3 dependency tree and building and wiring `@objectstack/cli` from this branch, which is more than linking the built package. The in-process probe above drives the same door and the same stage.

## Ablation

The ablation restores today's cut-before-classify order with one mutation in `verify.ts`. It goes through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (WRAP mode, its own exit, INT and TERM trap, plus a shell trap that runs `git checkout HEAD --` on the absolute path):

- Before the mutation, the line read `const text = await created.text();`. The mutation made it `const text = (await created.text()).slice(0, 280);`.
- The anchor was hit 1 time and dropped to 0. The replacement count went from 0 to 1. The blob moved from `d8fe2c05c833` to `d9528c3cad95`.
- With the mutation, `vitest run src/verify.create-refusal-verdict.test.ts` gave **1 failed, 4 passed**. The one red is the long-message case, `expected status "needs-fixture", received "create-failed"`. All four controls stayed green.
- After the restore, the blob read `d8fe2c05c833`, which equals HEAD. `git diff HEAD` was empty and `git status --porcelain` was empty.

The test imports `./verify.js` from source (a relative import, so there is no `dist/` resolution), so no rebuild leg was owed.

## Controls

The new test file is `packages/verify/src/verify.create-refusal-verdict.test.ts`. It uses a stack double (`apiAs` only, the same double pattern `reference-shape.test.ts` uses) and boots nothing. It has 5 cases, and all pass on HEAD:

1. A 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` whose message runs past 280 characters is `needs-fixture`, and `detail` equals the first 280 characters of the body. The fixture asserts its own precondition: the code key starts after character 280.
2. Control: a short 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` is `needs-fixture`.
3. Control: a 500 `INTERNAL_ERROR` is `create-failed`.
4. Control: a 400 `INVALID_FIELD` is `create-failed`.
5. Control: a 400 non-JSON `Validation failed: ...` body is `needs-fixture`. This exercises the full-text fallback.

## Local verification (HEAD `3bcc4ae59`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` (the whole package suite, under the shared lock) gave 44 test files and 376 tests passed, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/verify typecheck` exited 0. It runs `tsc --noEmit` and then `check:test-typecheck`, which reported "0 file(s) / 0 error(s)". `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new test file (1 hit). For comparison it lists 44 verify test files and 100 `packages/core/src` files.
- eslint (`--no-inline-config`) over `verify.ts` and the new test exited 0, with 0 errors and 0 warnings. The JSON output confirms both files were linted.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 63 commands. All 63 were run with each exit code captured before any pipe, and all exited 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3, unbuilt packages elsewhere in the tree). It was re-run after a full `turbo run build` (75 of 76 tasks cached) and exited 0.
- The `--ran` reconciliation read: `63 derived, 63 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (a derived zero, all 63 with recorded exit codes).
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`), the full union, was run at `3bcc4ae59` (the final commit) and exited 0 with no findings printed.

## Acceptance notes

- A JSON 400 whose top-level `code` is something other than `VALIDATION_FAILED`, but whose prose contains "Validation failed", now reads `create-failed`. The old pattern over the cut made it `needs-fixture`. On the `/data` create door, the only producer that writes that phrase into the flat envelope is the `VALIDATION_FAILED` arm itself (`data-error-classification.ts`). The other producers of the phrase are other doors: plugin-auth's adapter, the import runner, and the CLI's own printers. So no answer the door gives today changes its verdict except the long-message case.
- There are no out-of-scope findings. No other verify stage cuts a body before it classifies it: the sibling stages parse the full text, and their `clip` is applied to stored detail only.
